title: Count Set Bits
statement:
Count how many bits are set to 1 in a 32-bit integer.

Contract
- `value` is any `int`. Treat it as an unsigned 32-bit pattern, so negative numbers have their
  sign bit and all other bits counted like any other bit.
- Return a number from `0` to `32`.
- `Integer.bitCount` and similar built-ins defeat the purpose of the exercise, so avoid them.
  The tests cannot enforce this.

Examples
- `countSetBits(11)` returns `3` because `11` is `1011` in binary.
- `countSetBits(0)` returns `0`.
- `countSetBits(-1)` returns `32` because every bit is set.
hints: Look at one bit at a time: the lowest bit is `value & 1`, and shifting moves the next bit into place.
Be careful with negatives: an arithmetic right shift keeps the sign bit, so use the unsigned shift or a fixed 32-step loop. There is also a trick that clears the lowest set bit in one operation.

Clearing the lowest set bit with `value & (value - 1)` removes exactly one bit per step. Intended complexity: O(1) per call (at most 32 steps) and O(1) space, so a batch of n calls costs O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: a single integer, for example: 11
